message.content:
The lion (Panthera leo) and the zebra (Equus quagga) belong to two very different mammalian orders—Carnivora and Perissodactyla, respectively. Their most recent common ancestor is therefore the ancestor of the entire clade that contains **all placental mammals** (Eutheria).  

- **Last common ancestor of the two species:** the last common ancestor of all placental mammals, which lived roughly 100 – 110 million years ago during the early Cretaceous.  
- **Phylogenetic context:** This ancestor gave rise to the major placental lineages that later split into the various orders we see today, including Carnivora (lions, dogs, bears, etc.) and Perissodactyla (zebras, horses, rhinos, etc.).  

So, in short, the lion and zebra share a common ancestor that is the last common ancestor of all placental mammals.

The lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus quagga) are both mammals, but belong to different orders: lions are Carnivora, zebras are Perissodactyla. Their common ancestor would be a more distant mammalian ancestor. The most recent common ancestor of all placental mammals is the last common ancestor of placentals, which is the ancestor of all eutherian mammals. But maybe they want the common ancestor of the two species: the last common ancestor of the families Felidae and Equidae. That would be the ancestor of the order Carnivora and Perissodactyla, which diverged from the other ungulate orders. The last common ancestor of all mammals is the ancestor of all placental mammals. But the last common ancestor of the two species is the ancestor of the clade that includes both orders, which is the ancestor of the clade that includes all placental mammals. So the answer: the last common ancestor of all placental mammals, which lived around 100 million years ago. So we can say: the last common ancestor of the lion and zebra is the last common ancestor of all placental mammals, which lived about 100 million years ago. Alternatively, we can mention the last common ancestor of the two orders: the ancestor of the clade that includes Carnivora and Perissodactyla, which is the ancestor of the clade that includes all placental mammals. So answer: the last common ancestor of all placental mammals.
